children.title: What Khao Hakka Is
children.summary: Khao Hakka is a downtown Toronto Indo-Chinese and Hakka restaurant with a simple, self-serve, no-fuss identity.
children.content: Khao Hakka - Toronto is a downtown Toronto restaurant serving Indo-Chinese and Hakka cuisine. Its public-facing pages describe it as a simple self-serve style, no-fuss spot offering street-style Desi Hakka eats. The restaurant's menu is built around familiar Hakka favorites such as momo, noodles, fried rice, chicken, seafood, and lunch deals.
children.section: About Khao Hakka/Restaurant Overview/What Khao Hakka Is

children.title: Where It Is
children.summary: Khao Hakka is located at 37 Sherbourne St, Toronto, ON M5A 2P6, in downtown Toronto.
children.content: Khao Hakka is located at 37 Sherbourne St, Toronto, ON M5A 2P6. The restaurant is in downtown Toronto and the business phone number listed on the site is +1 (416) 504-5426.
children.section: About Khao Hakka/Restaurant Overview/Where It Is

children.title: Hours and Status
children.summary: Posted business hours and the site's closed-now messaging.
children.content: Khao Hakka's posted hours are Monday to Thursday 11:00am to 9:00pm, Friday 11:00am to 11:00pm, Saturday 4:00pm to 11:00pm, and Sunday 4:00pm to 9:00pm. The website also shows a closed-state message when ordering is disabled.

children.title: Catering and Contact

children.content: Khao Hakka's Linktree says it is a simple self serve style no fuss Indo-Chinese spot offering street style Desi Hakka eats. It also lists a catering menu and gives a contact number for catering and general queries: 416-504-5426. The profile note also says the meat is halal.

children.title: Main Menu Sections
children.summary: The menu is organized into Momo, Vegetarian, Chicken, Seafood, Fried Chicken Lollipop, Fried Rice, Noodles, Triple Schezwan, Meal for 2, Lunch, and Drinks.
children.content: The Khao Hakka menu is organized into these main sections: Momo, Vegetarian, Chicken, Seafood, Fried Chicken Lollipop, Fried Rice, Noodles, Triple Schezwan, Meal for 2, Lunch, and Drinks. The homepage also highlights these as the restaurant's core categories.

children.title: Menu Labels and Styles
children.summary: The menu uses spicy and vegetarian labels to help guests identify dishes quickly.
children.content: Khao Hakka's menu includes visual labels for spicy dishes and vegetarian dishes. That makes it easier for guests to scan the menu quickly and identify heat level or vegetarian-friendly items at a glance.

children.title: Example Dishes
children.summary: A few representative dishes and price points visible on the public menu.

children.title: Popular Dishes
children.summary: Publicly visible examples include Bombay Chicken, Momo, fried rice, noodles, and meal combos.
children.content: The public menu shows Bombay Chicken at $15.00 as a homepage best seller. Other visible dishes include Vegetable Steamed Momo at $13.00, Chicken Chilli Momo at $16.00, Hakka Fried Rice at $13.00, Hakka Noodles at $13.00, and Meal for 2 at $35.00.

children.title: Lunch Deals
children.summary: Lunch items are served from 11:00 to 16:00 and include rice, noodles, and combo meals.
children.content: The menu includes a lunch section labeled Lunch (11:00-16:00). Visible examples include Lunch-1 Egg Fried Rice at $12.00, Lunch-4 Chicken Hakka Fried Rice at $14.00, Lunch-8 Chicken Hong Kong Noodles at $14.00, and multiple vegetarian and chicken combo options.

children.title: Indo-Chinese Identity
children.summary: Khao Hakka serves Indo-Chinese and Hakka cuisine with a street-style Desi Hakka feel.
children.content: Khao Hakka serves Indo-Chinese and Hakka cuisine. The restaurant describes itself as a street-style Desi Hakka spot, which points to a bold, savory menu with familiar Chinese-Indian flavors rather than fine-dining style plating.
children.section: Food Style and Highlights/Cuisine Profile/Indo-Chinese Identity

children.title: Vegetarian and Halal Notes
children.summary: The menu includes vegetarian options and the public Linktree says the meat is halal.
children.content: The public menu includes a full Vegetarian section, and the restaurant's Linktree says the meat is halal. Guests looking for vegetarian dishes have several visible options across starters, mains, fried rice, noodles, and lunch deals.

children.title: Menu Coverage
children.summary: The menu spans momos, noodles, fried rice, chicken, seafood, and combo meals.
children.content: The visible menu coverage suggests a restaurant built around comfort-friendly Hakka staples: momos, vegetarian plates, chicken and seafood entrees, fried rice, noodles, quick lunch deals, and combo meals for sharing. That is a strong fit for casual dine-in or takeaway ordering.
